quote: And I shall have some peace there, for peace comes dropping slow, / Dropping from the veils of the morning to where the cricket sings; / There midnight’s all a glimmer, and noon a purple glow, / And evening full of the linnet’s wings.
source: W. B. Yeats, The Lake Isle of Innisfree, the second stanza, lines 5 to 8, The Rose (1893)

evidence.where: the Project Gutenberg text of The Collected Works in Verse and Prose of William Butler Yeats, Vol. 1, downloaded and read line by line this run; the contents place the poem at page 154 under the section heading THE ROSE
evidence.edition: Collected Works in Verse and Prose, Vol. 1, Shakespeare Head Press, 1908, reproducing the text of The Rose
evidence.locator: the second stanza, lines 5 to 8 of twelve

reason: All four lines match the scanned text word for word and point for point, including the semicolon at the end of line 6 and both apostrophes. First printed in the National Observer on 13 December 1890 and collected in The Rose, both confirmed. Yeats has no other line in the year.
